So the market appears to imply new-mine CAPITAL cost inflation of roughly 4.0% to 7.6% a year since April 2024. INDICATIVE CROSS-CHECK WITH ITS BASIS MISMATCH NAMED: First Quantum embeds 2.5%/yr of compounding US-dollar inflation in its own 2027-28 cost guidance [2026-01-15, PRIMARY], so the market-implied rate is 1.6x-3.0x what a producer books forward - BUT FQM's 2.5% is OPERATING-cost inflation while the market-implied figure is CAPITAL-cost inflation; these are different series and mining capital-goods inflation has historically run above operating inflation, so the comparison is INDICATIVE, NOT MATCHED (CLAUDE.md 15). THE MODEL CANNOT UNIQUELY INVERT PRICE TO ONE ASSUMPTION, SO THE SET IS STATED: (1) the incentive price is understated by 4.0-7.6%/yr of capital inflation - not verifiable, no capital-cost index reached; (2) a deficit deep enough to ration demand above the incentive price - UNEVIDENCED, the supply-demand module records the full-year 2026 balance direction as NOT ESTABLISHED (+96 kt vs -125 kt, opposite signs, 221 kt gap) with a realised Q1-2026 SURPLUS of +396 kt; (3) a location premium not a global scarcity premium - the COMEX leg carries ~+US$547/t (+3.8%) into an undated US Section 232 refined decision with 69.8% of visible copper in US warehouses, but removing it still leaves the LME leg US$1,251-2,251/t above the band, so location cannot be the whole answer and is not sized; (4) the incentive anchor simply does not bind at either horizon (10-20 year supply lead) - mechanically the strongest. NO SINGLE ASSUMPTION IS CHOSEN. STATISTICAL ROW, CONTEXTUAL, NOT VALIDATED.
